coverage_limits: ScienceDirect (Elsevier: Computers & Education, CAEAI, CAEO, Learning and Instruction, Thinking Skills and Creativity, IJME) and Taylor & Francis pages (ILE, SHE, JRTE, CALL, IETI) blocked scripted access and showed bot checks in the browser, which I did not attempt to pass; for many of these, abstracts were unavailable in Crossref/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar, so about a dozen records (mostly Thinking Skills and Creativity and some Computers & Education/L&I items) are included from titles alone with design and N marked unconfirmed. OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and the arXiv API hit shared rate limits (HTTP 429), so the OpenAlex boolean search returned only its first 200 of 212 results and no further OpenAlex free-text passes were run. The Crossref ISSN route returned Educational Technology & Society (1436-4522/1176-3647) as empty, so ET&S was covered only through ERIC. Web searches kept surfacing new small-venue studies (conference papers, regional journals) up to the end, so the eight-consecutive-empty-queries stopping rule was not reached; regional non-English journals (Chinese, Arabic, Turkish, Indonesian, Thai) and Frontiers/MDPI/Sustainability were sampled only through web and ERIC searches, not listed exhaustively. Many education studies measure creativity with scales that may be self-report; where the abstract did not say, the record is kept and flagged in 'evidence'.

candidates.title: Is Chatgpt a menace for creative writing ability? An experiment
candidates.task: creative writing essays (university students)
candidates.evidence: 600 students from 10 universities were split into a control group and an experimental group that used ChatGPT in their creative writing; essays were scored for originality, content presentation, accuracy and elaboration, and the authors report a detrimental association of ChatGPT use with these creative-writing dimensions. Random assignment is not stated.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing with robot–LLM integration: The interplay of embodiment, AI creativity and user engagement
candidates.task: collaborative creative writing with robot or screen LLM partners
candidates.evidence: 150 undergraduates wrote collaboratively under five conditions (human-human; computer or robot partner driven by a high- or low-creativity LLM); originality, imagery, voice and semantic flow were scored by expert raters and computational measures. Allocation procedure not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Generative AI: A double-edged sword for creative thinking learning — Evidence from facial expressions and fNIRS
candidates.task: design brainstorming and TRIZ tasks
candidates.evidence: 128 participants were split into a generative-AI design group and a traditional design group and completed divergent brainstorming and TRIZ design tasks; creativity output scores were higher with generative AI, alongside facial-expression and fNIRS measures. Abstract not accessible from the publisher; design details from the university news release (search snippet) and title.

candidates.title: The effects of critical thinking intervention on reliance behaviors, problem-solving quality, and creativity during human-Generative AI collaborative learning
candidates.task: problem-based learning tasks with generative AI
candidates.evidence: 226 students working with generative AI in problem-based learning were assigned to a critical-thinking intervention or a comparison condition (both used GenAI); outcomes include reliance behaviours, problem-solving quality and creativity. A variant-of-AI-use comparison; random assignment not stated in the available abstract text.

candidates.title: Student-AI collaborative creative Problem-Solving: The role of human agency
candidates.task: student-AI collaborative creative problem solving
candidates.evidence: Computers & Education study of student-AI collaborative creative problem solving that examines the role of human agency; the title indicates a comparison of agency configurations with creativity outcomes. Abstract not accessible (publisher blocked scripts; not in Crossref/OpenAlex), so design and N are unconfirmed; included for recall.

candidates.title: The influence of artificial intelligence generated content-based problem-solving on engineering students’ creativity: a controlled experimental study
candidates.task: engineering creative problem-solving course; CEDA test
candidates.evidence: Engineering students in a 2-month course either used AIGC tools for creative problem solving (n = 54) or traditional methods (n = 59); creativity was assessed pre and post with the Creative Engineering Design Assessment (fluency, flexibility, originality, usefulness), with larger gains in the AIGC group. Assignment method not stated; whether the post-test was completed without AI is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Enhancing design ldeation: comparing AIGC-engaged and traditional brainstorming in educational contexts
candidates.task: industrial design brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 21 undergraduate industrial design students divided into AIGC-engaged brainstorming and traditional brainstorming groups; creative outputs were rated on novelty, feasibility, correlation and utility.

candidates.title: Exploring AI-enhanced design education in China: a quasi-experimental study of traditional, chatbot-assisted, and fully integrated AIGC conditions
candidates.task: book design course (visual communication design)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 100 visual communication design students in three instructional configurations (traditional, chatbot-assisted, fully integrated AIGC); the fully integrated AIGC condition had higher AI-supported design product performance (pre/post), plus self-efficacy and role clarity.

candidates.title: Integration of AI GPTs in music education and their impact on students’ perception and creativity
candidates.task: piano teaching sessions; TTCT
candidates.evidence: 566 conservatory music students in an AI (ChatGPT) intervention group or a control group; creativity was assessed with two forms of the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking before and after, with a significant increase in the AI-intervention group. Allocation method not stated.

candidates.title: From text to moving image: Evaluating generative artificial intelligence text-to-video models for pre-writing idea generation in language instruction
candidates.task: pre-writing brainstorming in language instruction
candidates.evidence: Two groups of college freshmen (experiment vs control); the experimental group saw GenAI text-to-video clips during brainstorming; assessment of brainstormed ideas showed more ideas generated in less time. N and allocation not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-enhanced natural language processing tools on writing proficiency: an analysis of language precision, content summarization, and creative writing facilitation
candidates.task: EFL writing with AI NLP tools, including creative writing facilitation
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest design with random assignment to AI-tool interventions targeting language precision, content summarization and creative writing facilitation; outcome is writing proficiency. Whether creativity of writing was scored separately is unclear from the abstract; included for recall.

candidates.title: Product design education: integration with artificial intelligence as one of the tools for increasing creativity
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education, 36(2)
candidates.task: product (subject) design education
candidates.evidence: Experimental group using integrated AI tools vs control group with traditional teaching in product design education; creativity scores differed significantly (t about 6.18) in favour of the AI group. N and allocation not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Emotional valence and arousal: the impact of AI-generated image stimuli on design creativity
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education, 35(3)
candidates.task: design ideation with AI-generated image stimuli
candidates.evidence: Two experiments manipulated the emotional valence and arousal of AI-generated inspirational images given to design learners; design creativity (e.g., originality of ideas) was rated. Compares variants of AI-generated stimuli rather than AI vs no AI; N not in the snippet available.

candidates.title: Investigating generative artificial intelligence’s role in logo design pedagogy: effects on learning experience and outcomes
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education
candidates.task: logo design conceptualization (graphic design students)
candidates.evidence: Compared traditional and GAI-assisted teaching in the conceptualization phase of logo design among novice and skilled graphic design students; GAI-assisted teaching increased the quantity, novelty and diversity of conceptual designs but had limited effect on design quality. N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI on collaborative problem-solving and team creativity performance in digital story creation: an experimental study
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education, 22(1)
candidates.task: digital storytelling creation (20 weeks)
candidates.evidence: Sixty university students were randomly assigned to create digital stories with GAI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Runway) or by traditional methods; collaborative problem-solving and team creativity performance were assessed with pre/post surveys and interviews (creativity measure may be survey-based).

candidates.title: Facilitator or hindrance? The impact of AI on university students' higher-order thinking skills in complex problem solving
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education, 22(1)
candidates.task: design problem; design sketches
candidates.evidence: Within-subject experiment with 40 university students using ChatGPT-4o in complex design problem solving; consensus assessment showed AI slightly enhanced originality and usefulness of design sketches, plus higher-order-thinking analyses.

candidates.title: Exploring students’ experiences and perceptions of human-AI collaboration in digital content making
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education, 22(1)
candidates.task: digital content contest on sociocultural issues
candidates.evidence: Experimental group using generative AI (prompt-literacy training) vs comparison group using conventional digital tools; creative problem-solving ability and curiosity were compared, with higher creative problem-solving in the GenAI group. Measurement type and N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Interaction between students and artificial intelligence in the context of creative potential development
candidates.task: fine arts, literary writing and fashion design programmes; TTCT-Figural
candidates.evidence: Students in three creative disciplines were divided into intervention groups that used ChatGPT-4 for idea generation and control groups with the standard programme; creative thinking was measured with the TTCT-Figural pre and post (a test taken without AI). N not in the abstract excerpt.

candidates.title: Enhancing student engagement and higher-order thinking in human-centred design projects: the impact of generative AI-enhanced collaborative whiteboards
candidates.task: design thinking course projects
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 65 students using a generative-AI-enhanced collaborative whiteboard vs a conventional platform in a design thinking course; the GAI group outperformed on creativity and critical thinking (pre/post tests) and engagement.

candidates.title: Enhancing student creative and critical thinking in generative AI-empowered creation: a mind-mapping approach
candidates.task: digital storytelling in an art course
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 45 university students: a mind-mapping-integrated GenAI-supported digital storytelling approach vs a conventional approach; creative and critical thinking outcomes. The comparison condition is truncated in the abstract (likely GenAI-supported without mind mapping).

candidates.title: AI-supported interactive learning environments and students’ AI-related digital competence and perceived innovation capability: longitudinal and experimental evidence
candidates.task: creative thinking task with supportive vs AI-substitutive interaction
candidates.evidence: Includes a randomized task-based experiment comparing supportive and AI-substitutive interaction modes with generative AI during a creative thinking task; supportive interaction produced greater improvement in originality (plus a longitudinal survey component). N for the experiment not in the abstract.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an interactive learning environment: supporting creative problem posing in teacher education
candidates.task: mathematical problem posing (pre-service teachers)
candidates.evidence: Case study: 24 pre-service mathematics teachers posed problems scored for fluency, flexibility and originality; the 12 lowest scorers revised problems with ChatGPT and then posed new problems in a post-test. No control group; included because creativity is scored on output before and after AI-supported work.

candidates.title: The Effects of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Creative Writing on Students’ Writing Motivation, Writing Anxiety, and Creative Writing Skills
candidates.task: creative writing (4th grade)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 41 fourth-graders: creative writing activities with ChatGPT for five weeks vs traditional paper-and-pencil; creative writing skills were assessed from students' texts, plus motivation and anxiety scales.

candidates.title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Primary School Students’ Writing Skills: The Impact of ChatGPT on Creative Writing and Writing Self-Efficacy
candidates.task: creative writing with ChatGPT feedback (4th grade)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with pre/post control groups (31 + 31 ten-year-olds) in which ChatGPT feedback supported creative writing; outcomes were a Creative Writing Product Evaluation Scale and writing self-efficacy.

candidates.title: Guiding Novice Programmers With CPS-GPT: A Prompt-Driven AI Assistant for Creative Problem Solving
candidates.task: creative problem solving in a programming course
candidates.evidence: A prompt-driven ChatGPT assistant integrated with creative problem solving (CPS-GPT) vs a comparison condition (conventional ChatGPT use implied); CPS-GPT improved creativity (d = .557), critical thinking and problem solving. N and allocation not in the abstract excerpt; compares AI configurations.

candidates.title: A Study on the Role of Midjourney, A Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool, in Enhancing Student Creativity in Illustration Design Classes
candidates.task: illustration design studio (Midjourney)
candidates.evidence: Parallel-group quasi-experiment in two sections of an undergraduate illustration studio (n = 162): Midjourney-based ideation workflow vs conventional non-generative workflow; baseline and final artefacts were rated for originality, appropriateness and elaboration, with process metrics and attention to homogenisation.

candidates.title: Evaluating the Effects of Personalised Learning on AI‐Assisted Design Performance, Creative Self‐Efficacy, and Engagement of High‐ and Low‐Performing College Design Students
candidates.task: college design projects (ChatGPT vs DeepSeek vs conventional)
candidates.evidence: Comparative quasi-experiment of personalised learning with ChatGPT-4 and DeepSeek among high- and low-performing college design students; AI-assisted design performance improved relative to conventional creative methods, plus creative self-efficacy and engagement. N not in the abstract excerpt.

candidates.title: Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit Human–AI Collaboration: How Supportive and Contrarian AI Personas Reshape Interaction
candidates.task: creative movie-plot task in triads
candidates.evidence: 224 university students were randomly assigned to 97 online triads that were human-only or included an undisclosed supportive or contrarian AI persona, completing an individual-group-individual creative movie-plot task; outcomes are discourse patterns, learner agency and experience. Whether plot creativity was rated is not stated in the abstract; included for recall.

candidates.title: Comparing the Impact of Individual‐ and Team‐Based ChatGPT Collaboration on High School Students' Cognitive Competencies in Programming Education
candidates.task: collaborative programming with ChatGPT (high school)
candidates.evidence: Compares individual- vs team-based ChatGPT collaboration in high-school programming education on cognitive competencies (the 4Cs, including creativity). How creativity was measured is not stated in the abstract excerpt; included for recall.

candidates.title: Integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching: An empirical study on self-efficacy and learning outcomes
candidates.task: product design ideation teaching with AIGC
candidates.evidence: Empirical study integrating AIGC into product design ideation teaching, examining self-efficacy and learning outcomes (cited by later work as an AIGC vs conventional comparison). Abstract not accessible; design, N and whether design creativity was scored are unconfirmed.

candidates.title: An experimental study on the impact of Generative AI on university students' emotions and performance in creative problem-solving tasks
candidates.task: creative problem-solving / design task with or without an AI assistant
candidates.evidence: Experimental study of generative AI on university students' emotions and performance in creative problem-solving tasks; the linked data record describes a quasi-experiment in design education varying AI-assistant availability with creative task performance and academic emotions. Abstract not accessible; N unconfirmed.

candidates.title: AI4Design: A generative AI-based system to improve creativity in design–A field evaluation
candidates.task: design course projects with AI4Design (ChatGPT + DALL-E)
candidates.evidence: Field evaluation of a ChatGPT/DALL-E based system meant to improve creativity in design students' course projects; whether a comparison group and rated creativity outcomes exist is not visible in the available abstract text. Included for recall; may be a system evaluation only.

candidates.title: Comparing AIGC and traditional idea generation methods: Evaluating their impact on creativity in the product design ideation phase
candidates.authors: Lin, Jiang, Deng, Bian, Fang, Zhu
candidates.task: product design ideation (AIGC vs traditional methods)
candidates.evidence: Compares AIGC-based and traditional idea generation methods on creativity in the product design ideation phase. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed (title only). Possibly related to the already-collected Lin (2026) traditional vs generative AI divergent-thinking study, but a separate 2024 article.

candidates.title: Augmentation or limitation? Generative AI’s influence on college students’ creative problem-solving
candidates.task: college students' creative problem solving
candidates.evidence: Study of generative AI's influence (augmentation vs limitation) on college students' creative problem solving. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed (title only).

candidates.title: Symbiosis or stagnation? Investigating the impact of AI on creativity in L1 Chinese writing
candidates.task: L1 Chinese writing
candidates.evidence: Investigates the impact of AI on creativity in L1 Chinese writing. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed (title only).

candidates.title: Enhancing human computer collaboration in design process: How AI-generated content elevates students’ creativity
candidates.task: design process with AIGC (students)
candidates.evidence: Examines how AI-generated content in the design process elevates students' creativity. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed (title only).

candidates.title: Compositional tools based on artificial intelligence for choral artistic education: Enhancing creative skills in choral arrangements
candidates.task: choral arrangement composition
candidates.evidence: AI-based compositional tools in choral artistic education and students' creative skills in choral arrangements. Abstract not accessible; design and N unconfirmed (title only).

candidates.title: A framework for collaborating a Large Language Model tool in brainstorming for triggering creative thoughts
candidates.task: brainstorming with an LLM tool
candidates.evidence: Proposes and tests a framework for collaborating with an LLM tool in brainstorming to trigger creative thoughts. Abstract not accessible; whether there is an AI vs no-AI comparison is unconfirmed (title only).

candidates.title: ChatGPT effects on cognitive skills of undergraduate students: Receiving instant responses from AI-based conversational large language models (LLMs)
candidates.task: research methodology course tasks (flipped classroom)
candidates.evidence: 125 Ghanaian undergraduates were randomly allocated to use ChatGPT for in-class tasks (n = 60) or traditional databases and search engines (n = 65); critical, creative and reflective thinking were measured pre and post with scales (the creativity measure may be self-report).

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students’ mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study
candidates.task: mathematical creativity task (college students)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment comparing college students who used ChatGPT to solve a mathematical creativity task with a control group that did not; ChatGPT had a positive effect on mathematical creativity and on self-efficacy and interest. Possibly related to, but distinct from, the already-collected Liu (2025) human-ChatGPT/Google/human co-creation study.

candidates.title: Investigating student engagement with personalised generative AI feedback: Effects on creative problem-solving and feedback uptake
candidates.authors: Chen, Huang, Han, Zhang, Lou, Zhong
candidates.task: creative problem solving with GenAI feedback
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment with 62 Chinese university students comparing personalised vs standard GenAI feedback on creative problem-solving performance and feedback uptake (an AI-configuration comparison). Possibly from the same group as the already-collected Chen (2025) personalized-GenAI creativity study, but a separate article.

candidates.title: Generative AI use in EFL writing: associations with originality, critical reasoning, and metacognitive engagement in a Turkish higher education context
candidates.task: timed argumentative essays with optional ChatGPT/Grammarly/QuillBot
candidates.evidence: 78 first-year EFL undergraduates wrote three timed essays with optional access to ChatGPT (idea generation), Grammarly and QuillBot; associations between AI use and originality (rubric ratings and TTCT originality subscale), critical reasoning and metacognition were examined. Not randomized.

candidates.title: Synergising Computational and Design Thinking in Design Education: A Dual‐Process Framework to Enhancing Creativity and Appropriateness
candidates.venue: International Journal of Art & Design Education, 45(3)
candidates.task: fashion pattern design with AI style transfer
candidates.evidence: Experiment on fashion pattern design in which AI style transfer extended human-originated concepts within a computational/design-thinking framework; creativity and appropriateness were assessed with eye-tracking, subjective ratings and expert evaluation. N and comparison conditions not in the abstract excerpt.

candidates.title: Enhancing Creative Confidence in Design Students Through Topology‐Preserving AI Scaffolding

candidates.task: early-stage design ideation (sketch-to-image scaffold)
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment comparing a topology-preserving generative AI (ControlNet) sketch-scaffolding workflow with static mood boards for design students; the main outcome is creative confidence (likely self-report). Included for recall; rated-output outcomes unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Inquiry-based learning in STEM education: the impact of generative AI-based Chatbots on primary school students’ problem posing ability in science
candidates.authors: Dai, Huang, Xiong, Yang, Zhang, Peng
candidates.task: science problem posing (3rd grade)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment: 97 third-graders randomly assigned by class to a GenAI chatbot group (n = 48) or a search-engine group (n = 49) during inquiry-based learning; outcome is problem-posing ability in science (a creativity-adjacent outcome).

candidates.title: Cultivating design creativity of vocational students: A model of project-based learning in AI-enabled immersive virtual environments
candidates.venue: Research and Practice in Technology Enhanced Learning, 22
candidates.task: vocational design projects in an AI-enabled immersive environment
candidates.evidence: Two-group quasi-experiment in a vocational school evaluating project-based learning in an AI-enabled immersive virtual environment (intelligent agents with real-time feedback) on students' design creativity. Whether the agents are generative AI and N are not stated in the abstract excerpt.

candidates.title: How Does Learner Prior Language Knowledge Play in GenAI-Assisted Project-Based Learning for Creative Thinking?
candidates.task: English picture-book creation (EFL, ages 13-15)
candidates.evidence: 10-week quasi-experiment with 118 Chinese EFL learners creating picture books with GenAI under supportive (examples, structured guidance) vs reflective (open-ended prompts) scaffolding; supportive scaffolding enhanced creative thinking for some prior-knowledge levels (AI-configuration comparison).

candidates.title: Is generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) a game changer for interdisciplinary collaborative learning in higher education?
candidates.authors: Xia, Weng, Huang, Li, Kin, Chiu
candidates.task: interdisciplinary collaborative design learning
candidates.evidence: 2x2 between-subjects factorial design with 176 university students (same- vs cross-discipline groups, with vs without GenAI); no difference in individual creativity by GenAI, while groups without GenAI showed higher group creativity (relevance, elaboration, originality). A correction notice exists (doi 10.1007/s10639-025-13878-x).

candidates.title: Impact of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) applications on creativity skills for college students
candidates.task: educational technology course with GAI tools
candidates.evidence: 50 educational technology students were randomly assigned to use GAI tools (ChatGPT, Bard, Copilot) for learning or to traditional instruction; creativity (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) was measured post-test with a validated 18-item scale (possibly self-report), favouring the GAI group.

candidates.title: Effects of ChatGPT use on undergraduate students’ creativity: a threat to creative thinking?
candidates.task: teaching-unit design assignments over 10 weeks
candidates.evidence: One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT for academic assignments for 10 weeks; creativity was measured with the CREA test before and after, finding no evidence of a negative effect. No control group.

candidates.title: How does generative artificial intelligence impact student creativity?
candidates.task: alternative uses test in a college creativity course
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study in a college creativity course using AUT data to assess the impact of ChatGPT-3 on students' divergent thinking (fluency, flexibility, elaboration, originality); reports both supportive and negative effects. Exact comparison structure and N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: EEG assessment of artificial intelligence-generated content impact on student creative performance and neurophysiological states in product design
candidates.task: 3-hour product design task (walking cane)
candidates.evidence: 64 third-year design students in two groups: AIGC tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion) vs traditional design software; creative performance was rated (AIGC higher, d = 0.55) with EEG measures of concentration and relaxation.

candidates.title: The impact of AI-assisted composition tools on cultivating creativity among music students in Guangdong province
candidates.task: music composition
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 120 music students in Guangdong (experimental group with AI-assisted composition tools vs control); compositions were assessed pre and post on nine dimensions including creative fluency and expressive range, favouring the AI group.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of a Training Program Based on Artificial Intelligence Tools in Developing Creative Problem-Solving Skills
candidates.task: AI-tool-based training programme; TTCT
candidates.evidence: 75 tenth-graders in three intact classes randomly allocated to classroom-based training, AI-tool-based training, or control; the Torrance Test of Creative Thinking was given pre, post and at follow-up. Article in Arabic; the English title given here is the journal's parallel title (Arabic title in the Crossref record).

candidates.title: The effect of STEM themed story writing training with artificial intelligence tools on the digital literacy and 21 st century skills of preservice teachers
candidates.task: STEM-themed story writing (pre-service teachers)
candidates.evidence: 36 pre-service Turkish teachers in experimental (n = 19, wrote stories with AI tools) and control (n = 17, wrote stories without tools) groups over eight weeks; stories were evaluated on textuality criteria (cohesion, coherence, informativeness and others), with digital literacy and 21st-century skills scales as main outcomes. Whether creativity per se was scored is unclear; included for recall.

candidates.title: Chat GPT como catalizador del pensamiento creativo
candidates.task: collaborative song writing with ChatGPT (ages 12-13)
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest study in a Chilean school: students aged 12-13 created songs collaboratively with ChatGPT; on the TTCT, flexibility and originality rose while fluency fell slightly. No control group described in the abstract. English parallel title: 'Chat GPT as a Catalyst for Creative Thinking'.

candidates.title: Inteligencia artificial en el aula: potenciando la resolución de problemas a través del pensamiento creativo
candidates.venue: Revista de Comunicación de la SEECI, 58
candidates.task: song creation with ChatGPT and BandLab (8th grade)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with eighth-graders who created a song over five sessions with ChatGPT and BandLab; fluency and flexibility measured with the Torrance test. Presence of a control group is unclear from the abstract. English parallel title: 'Artificial intelligence in the classroom: empowering problem solving through creative thinking'.

candidates.title: The Use of Prompt Engineering in ChatGPT to Improve the Ability to Write Ethnoliteracy-Based Fiction Stories in Elementary Schools: A Quasi-Experimental Study
candidates.task: ethnoliteracy-based fiction story writing (5th grade)
candidates.evidence: Nonequivalent control group design with 50 fifth-graders: fiction-writing lessons with structured ChatGPT prompting vs conventional lessons; a pre/post story-writing test scored story-writing indicators and integration of cultural elements.

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co‐Creation
candidates.task: AUT, consequences and problem-solving tasks
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment with 202 German participants in four conditions (human-human dyads, human-Internet, human-AI with basic or specific instructions) across four creativity tasks; the human-human condition scored higher on several tasks. Assignment procedure not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Designing an integrated concept mapping and generative AI approach to develop pre‐service teachers' digital storytelling project outcomes and critical thinking
candidates.task: digital storytelling projects (pre-service teachers)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 62 pre-service teachers: integrated concept mapping + generative AI (n = 30) vs standalone generative AI (n = 32); digital storytelling outcomes improved, including the 'innovation' dimension; critical thinking gains favoured the control group (AI-configuration comparison).

candidates.title: ChatGPT and Me: Collaborative Creativity in a Group Brainstorming with Generative AI
candidates.task: group product brainstorming (graduate engineering course)
candidates.evidence: 33 graduate students in teams of 4-5 brainstormed product ideas; in select groups ChatGPT was added as a team member; analyses of logs and ideas found ideas generated with ChatGPT were perceived as more creative and that ChatGPT use did not necessarily homogenize ideas.

candidates.title: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education
candidates.venue: International Conference on Creativity, Management, Education, Technology and Sciences Conference 2026 Proceedings
candidates.task: creative tasks in Vietnamese higher education
candidates.evidence: 480 undergraduates at three Vietnamese universities in three randomized conditions (unaided control, unconstrained GenAI access, structured prompt-guided scaffolding); unconstrained AI raised fluency but reduced originality (d = -0.58), while structured scaffolding gave better creativity profiles.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing through AI-powered co-creation with cognitive and emotional outcomes
candidates.task: EFL creative writing with AI writing assistant
candidates.evidence: 92 intermediate EFL learners were divided into a high-AI-support group (comprehensive AI-generated feedback), a low-AI-support group and a conventional-instruction control group; creative writing skills and emotional outcomes were measured pre and post.

candidates.title: Fostering children’s creativity through LLM-driven storytelling with a social robot
candidates.task: storytelling with a social robot (children)
candidates.evidence: Two studies with children (32 aged 5-10; 93 aged 7-9) interacting with a robot driven by a GPT-3 model fine-tuned to behave creatively or non-creatively; children's stories were scored for fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality, with gains in the creative autonomous-robot conditions. Children were balanced across conditions on pre-test creativity.

candidates.title: Assessment of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Storytelling for Enhancing the Ideation Process at the Individual Level
candidates.venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Creative Technologies, 11
candidates.task: alternative uses test and creative storytelling (polytechnic students)
candidates.evidence: Ten polytechnic students in two groups, one collaborating with ChatGPT, completed Guilford's alternative uses test and a creative storytelling task; AI raised fluency and flexibility (and originality) on the AUT but not in story writing.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
other_versions: Working Papers, Department of Economics, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, No. 16/2026
candidates.task: open-ended creative writing task (lab experiment)
candidates.evidence: Laboratory experiment in which participants were randomly assigned to access to a large language model (ChatGPT) or not for an open-ended writing task; independent evaluators rated creative performance; gains are driven by active use and peak at about eight queries. Also issued as Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Department of Economics working paper 16/2026.

candidates.title: AI vs Human Writers: A Comparative Analysis of Story Rewriting through Readability Metrics
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology in Education and Science, 10(2)
candidates.task: story rewriting
candidates.evidence: Compares narratives rewritten by GenAI (ChatGPT, Gemini) with human-written stories on readability, verbosity, lexical density and lexical diversity; no person receives AI help.

candidates.title: A linguistic comparison between ChatGPT-generated and nonnative student-generated short story adaptations: a stylometric approach
candidates.task: short story adaptations (ESL students vs ChatGPT)
candidates.evidence: Compares 15 short-story adaptations written by nonnative ESL university students with 15 ChatGPT-generated adaptations of the same stories on content and stylometric features (length, lexical choice, word frequency).

candidates.title: Unraveling Creativity Through Variability: A Comparison of LLMs and Humans in an Educational Q&A Scenario
candidates.task: educational Q&A texts (LLM vs human)
candidates.evidence: Quantifies the 'creativity' of LLM-generated text as variability and compares it with human-written answers in an educational Q&A scenario aimed at pre-school/primary contexts.

candidates.title: When ChatGPT Writes Your Research Proposal: Scientific Creativity in the Age of Generative AI
candidates.task: research proposal generation (experimental psychology)
candidates.evidence: Compares ChatGPT-generated and graduate-student-written research proposals (hypotheses, experimental designs, justifications) for a fictitious scenario on scientific creativity criteria.

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT know what robots are thinking? - Evaluation of human-created vs. AI-generated scientific ideas
candidates.authors: Eymann, Lachmann, Hekele, Ashok, Berns, Czernochowski
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Annual Conference of the European Association of Cognitive Ergonomics
candidates.task: scientific idea generation (human vs AI)
candidates.evidence: Evaluates human-created vs ChatGPT-generated scientific ideas; context comparison of AI and human output. Abstract not available in Crossref; details from title.

candidates.title: Prompting for creative problem-solving: A process-mining study
candidates.task: creative problem solving with ChatGPT (prompt process mining)
candidates.evidence: Process-mining analysis of students' prompting while solving a creative problem-solving task with ChatGPT (follow-up to the Urban et al. 2024 experiment), relating prompting patterns to solution creativity within the AI condition. Abstract not accessible; included for recall.

candidates.title: Unpacking the relationships among key factors in the effectiveness of inquiry-based learning: What changes does ChatGPT bring?
candidates.venue: Journal of Research on Technology in Education
candidates.task: inquiry-based learning (high school)
candidates.evidence: 462 Taiwanese high-school students in traditional vs ChatGPT-assisted inquiry-based learning compared with ANCOVA and PLS-SEM; ChatGPT improved problem-solving skills but had limited impact on critical thinking and creativity (creativity measure not stated in the snippet).

candidates.title: Human, AI, and collaborative writing in computer science: a multilayer linguistic analysis of university students’ prompt-driven text production
candidates.task: writing and summarization tasks (computer science students)
candidates.evidence: 81 university students produced texts under human-only, AI-only and AI-human collaborative formats with four prompt strategies; text quality, semantic consistency and discourse structure were analysed. Whether creativity or diversity was measured is unclear; included for recall.

candidates.title: Utilizing AI Applications to Enhance Descriptive and Narrative Writing Skills of EFL Student Teachers
candidates.task: descriptive and narrative writing (EFL student teachers)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experimental study of ChatGPT and other AI writing applications on EFL student teachers' descriptive and narrative writing, with rubrics that include fluency, accuracy and originality (design details from search snippet; N unconfirmed).

candidates.title: The impact of Midjourney on students’ design and design process: an exploratory study
candidates.venue: Designing Retail & Services Futures Colloquium 2025: Sustainable Retail and Services Futures
candidates.task: retail interior design studio (Midjourney)
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study across three cohorts of master students in retail interior design, with the 2022-23 cohort (no AI) as control and later cohorts using Midjourney; reports effects on fluency and visual development of initial designs (from search snippet; N unconfirmed).

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Chinese Poetry Instruction
candidates.venue: International Journal of Online Pedagogy and Course Design, 15(1)
candidates.task: Chinese poetry writing with AI-generated images
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study using text-to-image and image-to-poetry generation in Chinese poetry instruction, with pre-, mid- and post-tests, surveys and analysis of student poems; whether a control group exists is unclear from the abstract.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in teaching creative writing: A systematic review in L1 and additional languages learning contexts
candidates.authors: Acosta Sánchez, Trujillo Sáez, Cantizano Márquez
candidates.venue: Porta Linguarum. Revista Interuniversitaria de Did´áctica de las Lenguas Extranjeras
candidates.task: systematic review: AI in teaching creative writing
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 21 experimental or quasi-experimental studies (2020-2025) on AI in teaching creative writing in L1 and additional-language contexts.

candidates.title: How Does Artificial Intelligence Shape Creative Thinking Processes in Educational Contexts? A Systematic Review of Cognitive Mechanisms
candidates.task: systematic review: AI and creative thinking processes in education
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 49 empirical studies (2022-2025) on how AI shapes creative thinking processes in educational contexts.

candidates.title: Can Generative AI influence creativity? A Meta-Analysis
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 AERA Annual Meeting
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI effects on student creativity
candidates.evidence: AERA 2026 roundtable paper: meta-analysis of 12 experimental studies on whether generative AI influences students' creativity; effects were significant mainly for self-report measures.

candidates.title: The Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on the Creative Thinking of Students
candidates.task: narrative review: GenAI and students' creative thinking
candidates.evidence: Report synthesizing recent literature on how generative AI affects students' creative and higher-order thinking across age groups (narrative review; low rigour).

candidates.title: Uncovering the effect of Gen AI-assisted learning on students’ creativity: A meta-analysis from quasi-experimental evidence
candidates.task: meta-analysis of quasi-experiments on GenAI-assisted learning and creativity
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of quasi-experimental evidence on the effect of GenAI-assisted learning on students' creativity. Abstract not accessible; number of studies unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Students’ writing skills and creativity in the age of artificial intelligence: A systematic review of creativity across diverse AI-supported writing contexts
candidates.task: systematic review: AI-supported writing and creativity
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of creativity across AI-supported writing contexts and students' writing skills. Abstract not accessible.

candidates.title: The cognitive impact of ChatGPT in higher education: A systematic review of critical and creative thinking outcomes
candidates.task: systematic review: ChatGPT and critical/creative thinking
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 67 empirical studies (2022-2025) on how ChatGPT affects university students' critical and creative thinking.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of generative AI in higher education design pedagogy: a meta-analysis of usage modes
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education
candidates.task: meta-analysis of GenAI usage modes in design pedagogy
candidates.evidence: Meta-analysis of 27 controlled studies (N = 2,847, 2023-2026) on generative AI in higher-education design pedagogy; overall d = 0.60, with creative ability the largest outcome category (d = 0.71).

candidates.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence on students’ higher order thinking: Evidence from a three-level meta-analysis
candidates.task: three-level meta-analysis of GenAI and higher-order thinking
candidates.evidence: Three-level meta-analysis of 19 experimental and quasi-experimental studies (k = 68, 2,347 participants) of generative AI effects on higher-order thinking, including creativity (overall g = 0.851).

candidates.title: The Applications and Roles of Generative Artificial Intelligence in School-Aged Student Creativity Development: A Systematic Review
candidates.task: systematic review: GenAI and school-aged students' creativity
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 57 empirical studies (2022-2026) on generative AI's applications and roles in school-aged students' creativity development (4P framework).

candidates.title: Evaluating AI-generated design solutions in a basic design studio
candidates.venue: International Journal of Technology and Design Education, 36(3)
candidates.task: basic design studio assignments (synthetic vs student solutions)
candidates.evidence: Text-to-image diffusion models generated synthetic solutions to design-studio briefs, refined with expert feedback, and these were evaluated alongside a control group in expert evaluation; about widening the solution space for students. Comparison details unclear.

candidates.title: The Effect of Generative AI on Design Students' Critical Thinking and Creative Achievement
candidates.task: graphic poster design (Midjourney/DALL-E vs traditional tools)
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment: 61 design students randomly assigned to two orders (traditional tools then AI tools, or the reverse) to create graphic posters; blind expert ratings of the creative works were higher with AI tools (partial eta squared = .545), while self-reported critical-thinking confidence was lower.

candidates.title: Inteligencia Artificial (IA) y su uso en la escritura creativa
candidates.task: micro-story writing (ChatGPT vs students)
candidates.evidence: 24 university students first had ChatGPT generate a micro-story with an ant character and then wrote their own after a didactic sequence; comparative textual analysis found the AI texts used conventional structures consistently, whereas student stories showed greater richness and diversity in characters, plots and endings.

candidates.title: Writing with, without and against the AI. Insights from a high school writing lab
candidates.task: short-story writing in a high-school writing lab
candidates.evidence: Exploratory study in one sophomore high-school class (Italian-speaking Switzerland): students wrote short stories alone or with ChatGPT 3.5, and ChatGPT-only stories were added; stories were compared quantitatively and qualitatively and evaluated by a same-age reading group, showing clear differences among the three types. Class size not stated in the abstract; DOI shown on the journal page did not resolve in Crossref when checked.

candidates.title: Training novices to think, or giving them LLMs? Evidence from an RCT
candidates.task: business case: marketing recommendations for a university merchandise store
candidates.evidence: 2x2 randomized controlled trial with 1,053 first-year undergraduates assigned to causal-reasoning training, ChatGPT Edu (GPT-4o) access, both, or neither; experts rated solutions, and the paper measures number of ideas and diversity of ideas across participants: ChatGPT raised evaluations and the number of ideas, while causal-reasoning training (not ChatGPT) increased the diversity of ideas.

candidates.title: GenAI-driven storytelling on senior secondary students' Generative AI literacy and writing skills: A mixed-methods research
candidates.venue: Research Papers in Language Teaching and Learning, 16(1), 79-95
candidates.task: narrative writing / GenAI-driven storytelling (Hong Kong senior secondary)
candidates.evidence: 76 secondary students randomly assigned to a five-week GenAI-driven storytelling intervention or traditional writing instruction; a rubric-based writing assessment before and after covered word usage, narrative structure and creativity, plus AI literacy and writing anxiety. Whether the post-test writing was done without AI is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: A New Muse: How Guided AI Use Impacts Creativity in Online Creative Writing Courses
candidates.venue: Oregon State Ecampus Research Unit, Research Fellows white paper (April 2025)
candidates.task: creative writing exercise in online introductory courses
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects study: 31 students in two online introductory creative writing courses did the same exercise without ChatGPT, with ChatGPT, and with ChatGPT plus instructor guidance; expert judges rated creativity with the Consensual Assessment Technique; ChatGPT alone did not change creativity, while guided use raised it, mainly for low-baseline students.

candidates.title: Advancing Creative Thinking: Construction and Application of a GenAI-Based Multi-Agent Collaborative System
candidates.task: creative problem solving over four task rounds (undergraduates)
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with four task rounds comparing a GenAI multi-agent collaborative system with a single-agent model for undergraduates' creative problem solving; creative thinking improved more in the multi-agent group, with the gap widening over tasks (AI-configuration comparison). N not stated on the abstract page; DOI shown by the publisher did not resolve in Crossref at the time of checking.

candidates.title: How Generative AI supports human in conceptual design
candidates.authors: Chen, Song, Guo, Sun, Childs, Yin
candidates.task: conceptual design tasks (novice designers)
candidates.evidence: Novice designers completed two conceptual design tasks with or without generative AI assistance (search snippet of the paper describes 20 participants randomly divided into ChatGPT, Midjourney, combined and human-only groups); analyses focus on which design stages AI supports and on idea outcomes. Creativity scoring details not on the abstract page; included for recall.

candidates.title: Scaffolding Creativity or Homogenizing Outputs? GPT-based Virtual TA's Impact on Student Ideation in Graduate Education
candidates.task: graduate course ideation on educational uses of a video game
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment comparing a 2023 cohort without and a 2024 cohort with JeepyTA, a GPT-powered teaching assistant; JeepyTA increased fully formed ideas, but JeepyTA-driven ideation showed creative homogeneity while student-driven ideas were more unique. N not stated.

candidates.title: The impact of generative AI on creative and structural academic writing: Enhancing originality, compliance, and autonomy in English language learning
candidates.venue: JEELS (Journal of English Education and Linguistics Studies), 13(2)
candidates.task: EFL creative and structural academic writing
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods sequential explanatory design with 80 undergraduates in experimental (GenAI) and control groups; creative writing was assessed for originality, cognitive flexibility and expressive innovation, with GenAI improving creative and structural writing. DOI shown on the journal page but not yet resolvable in Crossref.

candidates.title: Floor Raiser or Ceiling Limiter? Differential Storytelling Outcomes with a Child-Centric GenAI System Across Individual Differences
candidates.task: children's storytelling (ages 7-12)
candidates.evidence: Within-subjects experiment with 40 children (grades 2-6) comparing a GenAI-assisted storytelling system with a traditional storyboard; GenAI improved creativity and richness ratings and narrowed the quality gap between children by 83.5% (convergence), while coherence and structure tracked baseline ability.

candidates.title: Does AI Homogenize Student Thinking? A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Structural Convergence in AI-Augmented Essays
candidates.task: student essays augmented by an LLM under three prompt strategies
candidates.evidence: 6,875 essays in five conditions (human-only, AI-only, three human+AI prompt strategies) show a quality-homogenization trade-off in essay structure; the human+AI essays were generated computationally by GPT-5-mini revising existing human essays (AIDE corpus), not by students using AI, so this is a simulation with human baseline texts.

candidates.title: The Crutch or the Ceiling? How Different Generations of LLMs Shape EFL Student Writings
candidates.task: secondary-school EFL compositions written with LLM assistance
candidates.evidence: Compares secondary EFL students' LLM-assisted compositions from before and after ChatGPT's release using expert scoring and metrics such as MTLD lexical diversity; advanced LLMs raised scores and lexical diversity for lower-proficiency learners, and more LLM assistance correlated negatively with expert ratings. Number of students and assignment not stated on the abstract page.

candidates.title: Generative AI Enhances Students' Critical Thinking but Cannot Improve Creativity
candidates.venue: European Conference on Educational Research (ECER 2025), Network 16
candidates.task: animation materials in a media art course
candidates.evidence: Conference abstract: 86 media art students randomly assigned to AI training plus generative tools (GPT-4o, Midjourney, DeepArtEffects), AI training plus traditional tools, or a control class; all created animation materials afterwards; no meaningful creativity improvement from generative AI, while critical thinking improved.

candidates.title: Exploring the Role of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Creative Thinking Processes: results from a preliminary study
candidates.venue: Journal article (venue not shown in the institutional repository record, Universita Telematica Pegaso IRIS)
candidates.task: authentic creative task reinterpreting a disciplinary text
candidates.evidence: Quasi-experiment with 56 undergraduates in two groups, one allowed GenAI during the analytical phases before creative production; no significant difference in creative performance, with a small positive trend for the GenAI group. Venue and DOI not shown in the repository record.

candidates.title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Students' Creativity
candidates.venue: Soaring: A Journal of Undergraduate Research, Vol. 2025, Article 4
candidates.task: poem writing
candidates.evidence: 33 students randomly assigned to brainstorm with ChatGPT or work independently before writing poems; poems were ranked for creativity and coded for strategies and unique vocabulary; AI users' poems were rated more creative. Undergraduate research journal.

candidates.title: Effects of AI-Generated Drawing on Students' Learning Achievement and Creativity in an Ancient Poetry Course
candidates.task: ancient poetry learning with GenAI drawing (high school)
candidates.evidence: Two high-school classes: an experimental class (n = 31) used a GenAI drawing mode to visualize poems and a control class learned conventionally; outcomes include learning achievement and creativity (measure not shown in the excerpt). Bibliographic data from the ERIC record; DOI not found.
